## Investigation findings

**Summary:** The degradation is latency only. No spans carry an error status or a 5xx code, in either the abnormal or the normal window. The slowdown comes from one fault: a fixed delay of about 1.6 s inside `ts-user-service` on the `getAllUser` code path. I found one root cause, not several.

### Affected endpoints
The slow requests are all `GET /api/v1/adminuserservice/users` (called from the UI) and the calls it fans out to. Each one takes about 1.61 s, against a normal ~10 ms.

| Service | Span | Abnormal avg | Normal avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| ts-ui-dashboard | GET /api/v1/adminuserservice/users | ~1.6 s (in the affected window) | ~10 ms |
| ts-admin-user-service | GET /api/v1/adminuserservice/users | 1613 ms (p95 1618) | 9.7 ms (p95 12.9) |
| ts-user-service | UserController.getAllUser | 1607 ms (p95 1613) | 3.3 ms (p95 4.9) |

There were 25 slow calls, all in a 4-minute window from 04:38:43 to 04:42:58 UTC on 2026-05-02. Every other endpoint is normal or faster than baseline.

### Root cause: ts-user-service, `UserController.getAllUser`
- In a representative trace (trace_id from a slow `getAllUser` call), `getAllUser` starts at 04:38:43.046. Its first child, `UserRepository.findAll`, starts at 04:38:44.647. That leaves a 1.6 s gap before the repository call.
- The DB work itself is fast: `findAll` takes ~6.8 ms and the `SELECT` takes ~5 ms.
- The log line `[getAllUser][Get all user]` is written at 04:38:43.046, the same moment the span starts. So the delay sits between the controller entry and the repository call.
- The gap is the same on every slow call (roughly 1603–1613 ms), which points to a fixed wait or sleep in the controller or service code, not to variable load or contention.
- Other `ts-user-service` endpoints are not affected. `getUserByUserId` is actually faster in the abnormal window (1.9 ms vs 2.8 ms), and the database layer looks normal.
- Resource metrics for the pod show no saturation: CPU ~0.04 cores, memory flat, no major page faults, and the deployment is available.

### Propagation
`ts-ui-dashboard` (GET /adminuserservice/users, 1.6 s) → `ts-admin-user-service` (GET /adminuserservice/users, 1.6 s, calls `getAllUsers`) → `ts-user-service` (GET /userservice/users → `getAllUser`, where the 1.6 s is spent). The 1.6 s is not added at any hop above `ts-user-service`; it originates there.

### Other observations (not causal for latency)
Several services show large increases in ERROR/WARN log volume: ts-route-service (994 vs 52), ts-verification-code-service (6345 vs 902), ts-travel2-service, ts-admin-route-service and ts-basic-service. Each of these uses a message template that also appears in the normal window ("Route not found", "Cookie not found", "No content"). Their trace latency and error status are unchanged, so I treat them as side effects of request volume or mix, not as a second fault.

### Confidence
High that the origin is `ts-user-service` `getAllUser`, with a fixed ~1.6 s delay before its repository call. I did not find a log message or metric that names the mechanism behind the delay. Reading the `getAllUser` code path (controller and any service-layer call before `findAll`) for a sleep, blocking lock, or synchronous external call is the next step.
